site.name: HuMed
site.tagline: Exploring the human side of healthcare at Yale
site.description: Yale's student organization at the intersection of humanities and medicine.

home.lead: HuMed is Yale's student organization dedicated to the intersection of humanities and medicine. Through symposiums, the HuMed Review, and community events, we examine how literature, ethics, history, and the arts shape the practice and experience of medicine.
home.heroImageAlt: Yale Undergraduate Humanities in Medicine Celebrations

pillars.title: Annual Symposium
pillars.description: Each year we host a symposium bringing together Yale students, faculty, and clinicians to discuss topics at the crossroads of humanities and medicine.

pillars.title: HuMed Review
pillars.description: Our student publication publishes essays, creative writing, and reflections on medicine, health, and the human experience.

pillars.title: Guest Speakers
pillars.description: Talks and conversations with clinicians, scholars, and alumni on the humanities, medicine, and the human experience in healthcare.

pillars.title: Study Breaks
pillars.description: Low-key gatherings during the semester — food, conversation, and a chance to recharge with the HuMed community.

items.title: Humanities in Medicine Celebrations 2026
items.description: Our annual symposium, themed "Healing, Narratives, and the Future of Medicine" — a fireside chat, panel, and workshop on creative expression and the human experience in medicine, with Yale faculty. Food and drinks provided.

items.title: Comics from the Heart
items.description: Explored medical storytelling through comics ahead of Valentine's Day and American Heart Month — cardiovascular health, medicine, and designing our own medical comic strips. Snacks provided.

items.description: Hot chocolate and ornament decorating to close out the semester.

items.title: HuMed Art Night at the Peabody
items.description: An afternoon at the Yale Peabody Natural History Museum — exploring the museum and practicing how art relates to medicine and science. Journaling and sketching supplies provided.
items.imageAlt: HuMed Art Night at the Peabody Museum

items.description: Discussion of prose, poetry, and the human experience at the intersection of faith, medicine, the arts, and the disadvantaged with Dr. Adjoa Boateng Evans YC '07, Assistant Professor of Anesthesiology at Duke University School of Medicine.

journal.submissionNote: Yale Undergraduate Humanities in Medicine Celebrations is excited to announce our call for submissions for the Yale Undergraduate Humanities in Medicine Review. We are looking for visual art, creative writing, or scholarly work at the intersection of the humanities and medicine, or art and science. All Yale community members welcome.

officers.lead: Our leadership team organizes symposiums, publishes the HuMed Review, and builds community around humanities and medicine at Yale.
officers.contactIntro: Interested in joining HuMed, submitting to the HuMed Review, or partnering on an event? Sign up on Yale Connect or reach out on Instagram — we'd love to hear from you.
